newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Coca-Cola Amatil first half seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Coca-Cola Amatil first half seen steady.

text.p: Australian soft drink group Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd is expected to post a slight improvement in net profit before abnormals for the first half to June 30 when it reports on Wednesday.
Analysts' forecasts centre around A$60 million, compared with a net profit for the same period last year of A$58.9 million, with some as high as A$70 million.
However, the result will be an improvement on the preceding weak half, particularly in Eastern Europe, where margins were hit by a battle for market share with PepsiCo Inc.
"They are coming off a very weak base in the second half of last year," a Sydney-based analyst said.
"(But) there are only so many price rises you can put through in a quarter so they are only starting now in some territories to price at the same level that they were this time last year."
C-C Amatil, a Coca-Cola Co anchor bottler owned 33.4 percent by Coke, has expanded rapidly in recent years, and now operates in 18 countries, mainly in Eastern Europe and Southeast Asia.
Overall sales are expected to show continued growth, although Australian sales may lag other regions.

Analysts will also be looking for signs of performance into the second half, when C-C Amatil will incorporate the soft-drink subsidiary of San Miguel Corp, acquired in a A$3.4 billion share swap deal which was finalised on July 1.
"The big interest will be in the full year result, with the Philippines deal, more so than this half," said a second Sydney-based analyst.
Investors will also watch for information about any impact in the second half from the severe flooding in Poland, such as disruptions to distributions systems.
Analysts, meanwhile, expect continued volatility in the group's share price, although somewhat moderated from the sharp swings of the past 12 months.

A share placement to the East Asian Kuok group, a profit warning, a disappointing full year result and the acquisition of Coca-Cola Bottlers Philippines Inc have seen the share price gyrate between A$18 and A$11.15.

The San Miguel deal -- which boosted market capitalisation by about 50 percent -- has lifted exposure to the volatile Philippine peso and put a substantial part of future earnings in the competitive Philippine soft-drink market.
The company's continued growth in other areas, such as Eastern Europe and Indonesia, where it recently opened its tenth bottling plant, has also helped change its profile.
"It's more volatile now, but that's to be expected given that it has a more volatile earnings base than it has ever had," said the first analyst.
"You are not going to see that solid 25 percent growth every year, some years it's going to be 40 and some years it's going to be five."
